files.purpose: The @MainActor @Observable ProviderRegistry is the app's single source of truth for every provider's install/sign-in state (ProviderStatus with its summary strings "Not installed", "Signed in as ...", "Signed in", "Not signed in", "Installed · <version>"), for each provider's model catalog (seeds for Claude, DeepSeek, Meta, Z.ai, Antigravity, Copilot, Command Code and Pi; live catalogs from the CLIs, ACP probes and APIs, cached under providerModelCatalogs with dates under providerModelCatalogDates), for slash-command lists per (provider, directory), plan limits, pay-as-you-go credits and banked-reset spending. It resolves each CLI's executable (custom path, PATH via LoginEnvironment.which, then per-provider fallback directories), builds its environment (PATH prefix, COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY, OpenCode MCP env, GEMINI_CLI_SYSTEM_SETTINGS_PATH), and runs the version/auth probes. New at B3 (1.7.0): it keeps the Claude Code and Codex CLIs current by running their own `update` subcommand at most every 12 hours (or forced after a turn fails with a too-old-CLI error), recorded under the new defaults key providerCLIUpdateDates, and the Claude live catalog now lends its versioned display name (e.g. "Opus 5.5") to seed rows other than Default.

CHANGED mergedClaudeCatalog (B3 :95-98): for a live row matching a seed id, `if option.id != "default", !option.name.isEmpty, option.name != option.id { kept.name = option.name }` runs before the efforts/detail/fastTier/defaultEffort merges. So a live Claude row now renames its seed row ("Opus" -> e.g. "Opus 5.5"), except the Default row, an empty live name, or a live name equal to its id. The comment says recipes pick the newest family member by name and a seed row named just "Opus" lost to the older "Opus 5" row. The doc comment at :87-89 still says the live row lends only effort levels, description and fast tier (stale comment upstream). This contradicts PR-PROVREG-138's expected_result ("A live row's name never replaces the seed's name").

NEW state (B3 :53-55): observable `updatingCLIs: Set<ProviderKind>` and the defaults key `providerCLIUpdateDates`. No view reads updatingCLIs anywhere in the B3 checkout (grep over *.swift finds references only in this file); it is published but unread, like signingIn and redeemingReset.
NEW updatesOwnCLI (B3 :477-479): true for exactly .claude and .codex.

NEW needsNewerCLI (B3 :482-490, nonisolated static): lowercases the message and returns true if it contains any of "or newer is required", "requires a newer version", "claude update", "codex update", "upgrade codex", "update codex". Used by ThreadRuntime.finishTurnUpdatingCLI to divert a failed turn into update-and-resend.

NEW updateCLIIfDue(_:force:) (B3 :496-522), exact order: (1) guard updatesOwnCLI, !CaptureRun.isEnabled, settings.binaryPath(for:) empty (a user-set binary is left alone) else false; (2) if updatingCLIs contains the provider: unforced returns false, forced polls every 500 ms until it clears; (3) reads providerCLIUpdateDates; unforced and last attempt < 12*3600 s ago (wall-clock seconds-since-1970 subtraction) returns false; (4) await LoginEnvironment.load(); no executable returns false without writing a date; (5) insert into updatingCLIs, defer remove; (6) before = cliVersion; run `<exe> update` in the temp dir, env = environment(for:), timeout 300, result and throw ignored; (7) write dates[rawValue] = now and persist (so a failed or timed-out update still waits 12 h unless forced); (8) after = cliVersion; nil or equal to before returns false; (9) else await refresh(provider), await loadCatalog(provider, force: true), return true. Note the dates dictionary is read before the awaits and written back whole afterwards, and the in-flight check precedes the LoginEnvironment await, so two unforced callers can both pass the gates; exact parity keeps this ordering.

NEW installedCLIVersion (B3 :525-529) and cliVersion (B3 :531-536): `<exe> --version`, timeout 30 s (the status probe version() uses 20 s), requires success, returns stdout trimmed of whitespace and newlines (no ANSI strip, no regex, stderr ignored), empty -> nil. The full trimmed text (e.g. a version plus product name) is what before/after compare and what ThreadRuntime shows in its "is up to date now (<version>)" notices.

Unchanged but shifted: everything else (seeds, init cache load, executable/environment resolution, signIn, refresh probes, catalogs, plan limits, credits, reset spending, slash commands, auth probes). signIn/signingIn/redeemingReset still have no reader or caller outside this file at B3, so PR-PROVREG-234/235/236 still hold; the dead guard in refreshPlanLimits (PR-PROVREG-237) is still dead, now at B3 :706 (B2 :627).
